The speaker can say the line “We’re invited guests of His Majesty, here for the feast.” (`guest`) to Guard (captain). It is said at `speak` (the default): its words reach everyone in the speaker's room (the wall partition the speaker stands in), and anyone in the next room within 30 feet of the speaker by the way through an open doorway (a closed door stops them), and whoever it is said to, wherever they stand. Whoever sees the speaker is told who said it; whoever the words reach and does not see the speaker hears the words — and which line it was, the roll, whether it worked and what it taught — from someone unnamed; whoever only sees it said learns neither the words, which line it was, whether it worked, nor what it taught; whoever the words do not reach may still notice a voice by passive Perception, never a whisper; the one it is said to is named only to those who see them. It is a checked line: it costs an action, one round of the world out of a fight.

The line “We’re invited guests of His Majesty, here for the feast.” (`guest`) is offered to a speaker only while the conversation `front-gate` is in one of the states `fresh` or `warned-troupe` (one state for the whole run, not per speaker).

Said to Guard (captain), the line “We’re invited guests of His Majesty, here for the feast.” (`guest`): winning it steps the conversation `front-gate` with the beat `admitted`, which moves it from `fresh` to `admitted` or from `warned-troupe` to `admitted`; missing it steps the conversation `front-gate` with the beat `guest-failed`, which moves it from `fresh` to `warned-guest` or from `warned-troupe` to `arrested` (the line is offered only in `fresh` or `warned-troupe`).

On a win of the line “We’re invited guests of His Majesty, here for the feast.” (`guest`), Guard (captain) answers “Then welcome. Through to the hall.”, at `speak`: its words reach everyone in Guard (captain)'s room (the wall partition Guard (captain) stands in), and anyone in the next room within 30 feet of Guard (captain) by the way through an open doorway (a closed door stops them), and whoever it is said to, wherever they stand and whoever sees Guard (captain) answer and caught none of the line is told only that Guard (captain) answered and what Guard (captain) is seen doing, and, if they see the speaker, sees the line said without its words.
